Technically speaking the OP's title is factually correct to call it a tube. The laser etching is being done on the outer casing of the suppressor, which is in fact a metal tube. It would be more specifically accurate to call it a suppressor, but on this matter the OP is technically correct.

Also, as the suppressor is built using a metal tube, it isn't factually correct to say that the two are completely different. Largely different would be more accurate... Since you wanted to split hairs.

For future reference, laser printing refers to the process of using an electromagnetic beam to create magnetically charged spots that toner powder will adhere too, then use heat to melt and bond the toner to the material being printed on. Whereas laser etching uses instead a subtractive process that removes material to create letters or other designs with the negative space.
